items.t: 48V mild-hybrid electrical system fault warning
items.job: Diagnose 48V system; replace belt starter-generator if it has failed
items.note: Audi says a sensor or network fault can cause this warning, so the starter-generator is not always the part to replace. Often covered by warranty on newer cars.

items.t: Water pump leaks coolant
items.job: Replace coolant pump and refill coolant
items.note: Owners report about $1,400 at a shop. Many replace the thermostat and PCV valve at the same time.

items.t: Thermostat sticks and causes overheating or slow warm-up
items.note: Labor is high because the supercharger has to come off to reach the thermostat.

items.t: Torn PCV valve causes oil burning and whistling
items.job: Replace crankcase pressure regulating (PCV) valve and update engine software
items.note: Audi's bulletin allows about 2.8-3.8 hours because the supercharger and fuel rails come off; the software update is about 0.5 hour of that. Owners on Audizine report shop bills of about $1,750 for the PCV alone.

items.t: Carbon buildup on intake valves causes rough running
items.job: Walnut-blast clean intake valves (supercharger or intake removed) with new intake gaskets
items.note: Hours start from Audi's bulletin time to remove the supercharger and fuel rails (about 2.3 hours) plus blasting time. Owners report about $500-$600 at independent shops and about $1,850 at a dealer. Shown for the supercharged 3.0T; the 55 TFSI may differ.

items.t: Timing chain rattle on cold start
items.job: Replace both upper timing chain tensioners with updated parts (transmission removed)
items.note: The chains sit at the back of this engine, so the transmission (and on some cars the engine) comes out. Audi bulletin 2039995/1 calls for updated left and right tensioners; dealer catalogs list them at about $180 and $238. Labor hours are not published, so hours are based on a dealer quote of about 40 hours and owner quotes of $4,500-$7,500 for the same 3.0T job on A6, A7 and Q7. Seals and fluids add to the parts total; worn chains or guides found during the job cost more.

items.t: Supercharger whine or grinding from worn bearing
items.job: Replace supercharger clutch pulley bearing (front of supercharger)
items.note: Parts are the genuine Audi pulley bearing (about $93 sale, $123 list). Hours are based on owner-reported shop quotes of 2-3 hours for supercharger pulley work on the same 3.0T. If the bearing inside the supercharger nose has failed instead, the supercharger needs a rebuild or replacement, which costs far more.

items.t: Rear spoiler error message or slow spoiler
items.job: Lubricate rear spoiler drive hinges (after checking them for corrosion)
items.note: Labor is from Audi's bulletin (about 0.2 hour, plus up to 0.2 hour of diagnosis); the lubricant costs little. If a weak 12V battery is the cause, price a battery instead.

items.t: Coolant loss from pump or thermostat housing (55 TFSI)
items.job: Coolant leak diagnosis (repair cost depends on the part found)
items.note: Cars still under Audi's warranty should go to a dealer.

items.t: Low coolant warning when the level is fine
Driver-assist and sensor warnings come and go
items.job: Diagnose warning and sensor fault codes
items.note: Repairs after diagnosis vary; ask about warranty and software updates first.

items.t: Rear suspension clunk or rattle over bumps
items.job: Replace worn rear control arm or shock absorber
